Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,
either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

Output verbosity levels (when explaining a specific item):
  Default:         Detailed view with scoped prompts (ID, session, tokens, intent, prompts, files)
  --short          Summary only (ID, session, timestamp, tokens, intent)
  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)
  --raw-transcript Raw transcript file (JSONL format)

Machine-readable export modes (additive surface for external consumers):
  --json           Metadata-only JSON. Lists checkpoints when no target is given;
                   emits a single checkpoint envelope when a target is supplied.
                   Transcript bytes are NEVER embedded in the JSON envelope.
  --transcript     Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes (JSONL) to stdout
                   for the selected session. Same bytes as --raw-transcript

  --session-index  Pick a session within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based).
                   Defaults to the latest session. Only meaningful with
                   --transcript or --raw-transcript.
  --limit          Cap the number of checkpoints returned by the list view.
                   Defaults to 100. When the cap is hit, a stderr note

## 🎯 What it is

entire-graph builds a **code graph** — nodes for files, packages, functions, classes, methods, types, routes, and resources; **30 relation types** for calls, construction, inheritance, field access, service boundaries, and config/infra dependencies — and answers structural questions from it:

- **Where is this defined?** → symbols
- **Who calls this / what does it call?** → neighbors, edges
- **Find the code for this task** → search (hybrid, ranked)
- **What changed, and what does it put at risk?** → diff / commit / checkpoint
- **Give me the whole graph** → snapshot

Everything is **deterministic** (pure tree-sitter static analysis — no LLM, no vectors, no similarity thresholds), **git-native** (every result keyed by `(repo, commit, tree)`, so it is content-addressed and cacheable per commit), and **100% local** (no keys, no network, no telemetry). It scales to millions of relations on one machine and releases memory after each build.

## 🔌 MCP & Entire Brain integration

**entire-graph is not itself an MCP server, and it exposes no MCP tools.** It is a local CLI plugin and a machine-readable **semantic provider**. There is nothing to configure as an MCP endpoint here, and no daemon to run.

MCP access to code intelligence comes from **Entire Brain** (`entire-brain`), a **separate** downstream product. Entire Brain ingests entire-graph's NDJSON output (`snapshot` / `symbols` / `edges`) into its own persistent store and is what exposes MCP tools to agents (`brain_search`, `brain_code`, `brain_impact`, `brain_context`, and so on). So the split is:

| Layer | Role | How you use it |
|---|---|---|
| **entire-graph** (this repo) | Deterministic graph engine + NDJSON provider | `entire graph <command>` on the CLI (see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)) |
| **Entire Brain** (separate) | Persistence, indexing, query, **MCP server** | MCP tools in your agent, backed by the graph above |

If you want MCP-style querying inside an agent, install and configure **Entire Brain** (its own docs) — entire-graph is the graph it builds on. If you just want direct, no-egress graph queries from an agent or the terminal, call `entire graph ...` directly; no MCP layer is required.

## ♻️ Refresh & keeping the graph current

entire-graph has **no watch mode, no daemon, and no file-watcher**, and it needs none. The graph is **deterministic and content-addressed by `(repo, commit, tree)`**, so "refreshing" is just re-running a query — the result reflects whatever state you point it at.

There are two modes, and neither can go stale on you:

- **Working tree (default).** Every `search`, `neighbors`, and `snapshot` re-reads your live files, so results always include your uncommitted edits. Nothing to refresh — just run the command again.
- **Committed tree (`--head`).** Results are cached by the git **tree hash** (under `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR`, or an explicit `--cache-dir`). Make a new commit and the tree hash changes, so the cache **automatically misses and rebuilds** — you can never read a committed-tree answer that is stale for that commit. `--no-cache` disables the cache entirely.

To warm the cache for a large repo before a latency-sensitive session, prebuild it once:

```sh
entire graph index --repo . --head --profile full --cache-dir /path/to/cache
```

Re-running `index` **is** the refresh: same tree → instant cache hit; changed tree → a fresh build. After that, `search` and `neighbors` on the same committed tree report the cache hit directly. This is the whole "keep it current" story — deterministic re-index, no background process.

## How plugins actually attach to Entire

It's dead simple — there's no RPC/daemon/protocol to learn:

- **`entire-plugin.yml`** is just `name:` + `description:` metadata (see `~/p/entire-graph/entire-plugin.yml` — two lines total).
- The real contract is a **binary named `entire-<name>`**, discovered on `$PATH` or copied/symlinked into `~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin` via `entire plugin install <path>`.
- `entire graph search ...` is just argv passthrough to `entire-graph search ...`. That's the whole API.
- There's also a **hidden, separate hook contract**: `entire hooks claude-code <event>` (session-start, session-end, stop, user-prompt-submit, pre-task, post-task, post-todo), wired into the *project's* `.claude/settings.json` by `entire agent add claude-code`. This is how entire tracks sessions/checkpoints as you work — independent of the plugin mechanism above.

So "rewrite gossamer to plug into entire directly" cashes out as: **ship `entire-gossamer` as a plugin binary**, installed the same way entire-graph is, invoked as `entire gossamer ...`.

## The bigger discovery: entire already does a lot of what gossamer reimplements

I checked what's actually installed (`entire 0.8.42`, logged in), and there's substantial overlap with gossamer's hand-rolled logic:

| Gossamer does this manually today | Entire already provides |
|---|---|
| Walks `entire/checkpoints/v1` tree, parses `metadata.json`/`full.jsonl` itself | `entire session list/info --json`, `entire checkpoint list/explain --json --transcript --full --generate` |
| Own SQLite index of sessions | `entire session info <id>` gives full state (agent, model, status, worktree, tokens, checkpoints) already |
| `witchcraft`-based local semantic search over transcripts | `entire checkpoint search` — hybrid semantic+keyword, server-side, also supports `--code` (searches code content) and cross-repo `--all-repos` |
| `gossamer resume <id>` (worktree lookup + relaunch) | `entire session resume <branch>` / `entire session adopt` already do worktree-aware resume |
| `gossamer new-session -b branch` | overlaps with `entire session resume`/`adopt` semantics |
| `gossamer attach`, `gossamer clean` | already thin wrappers over `entire attach`/`entire clean` — no change needed |
| Its own global Claude Code `SessionStart`/`Stop` hooks (`~/.claude/settings.json`) | entire installs its **own**, richer, project-scoped hook set (`entire hooks claude-code ...`) covering session-start/end, stop, prompts, task pre/post — running in parallel, duplicating session-boundary tracking |
| Summarizing "what happened" for browsing | `entire recap`, `entire dispatch`, `entire activity`, and `entire labs {blame,why,experts}` (line-level provenance from checkpoints) |

Gossamer's local semantic search is cloud-free (no login/network needed); `entire checkpoint search` requires `entire login` and hits a server. That's a real, deliberate tradeoff, not a strict downgrade — witchcraft is worth keeping *if* offline/private search matters to you.

## What gossamer still uniquely offers

- The **cross-repo catalog + TUI** (`gossamer repo`, worktree list, `gr` shell integration) — entire's CLI is single-repo-scoped (auto-detects from cwd), it has no "browse everything I've ever tracked" view.
- **Fully local, no-auth semantic search** via witchcraft.
- The shell ergonomics (`gr` function, clipboard-copy prompt on launch).

Everything else — indexing checkpoint branches, parsing transcripts, session lifecycle, hook plumbing — is now redundant machinery gossamer built before `entire session`/`entire checkpoint` matured.

## What a rewrite would look like

1. Rename the binary to `entire-gossamer`, add a two-line `entire-plugin.yml`, install via `entire plugin install`. Now it's `entire gossamer repo` / `entire gossamer search` etc.
2. Delete the checkpoint-branch tree-walking and JSONL parsing (`ingest/`, `is_meta_path`, `commands/index.rs`/`refresh.rs`) — replace with shelling out to `entire session list --json`, `entire session info --json --transcript`, `entire checkpoint list/explain --json`.
3. Drop gossamer's own Claude Code hooks entirely — rely on entire's existing `entire hooks claude-code session-start/stop` project hooks, and have `entire-gossamer` read state from entire's own store instead of duplicating hook installation.
4. Decide witchcraft's fate: keep as an **opt-in local search backend**, defaulting to `entire checkpoint search --json` when logged in, falling back to witchcraft when offline/not authed.
5. Keep and lean into the actual differentiator: the SQLite catalog becomes a thin **cache/index over entire's session list** (for the cross-repo TUI), not a primary source of truth.

This is the same shape as entire-graph itself: a small, focused plugin binary that wraps/extends entire's native surface rather than parallel-implementing it.

You're right, I collapsed the distinction too fast. Looking at the actual source, gossamer's resume path already does the right thing:

`show::resume_via_entire` (src/commands/show.rs:1312) creates the worktree itself (`create_resume_worktree`) if the target branch isn't checked out, then shells out to `entire session resume <branch>`, captures the command it prints on stdout, and `exec()`s that. It only falls back to that path after trying a faster `claude --resume <id>` directly (`resume_session`, show.rs:1388) when it can find the session's cwd/branch from the local JSONL. So `entire session resume` isn't a launcher — it's a **resolver that hands back the exec command**, and gossamer is the thing that actually knows how to get the worktree into the right state first. That's genuinely complementary, not a wrapper to delete.

Same story for `new-session`: `entire session resume`/`adopt` operate on sessions that already have a worktree. Gossamer's `create_worktree` (new_session.rs) is what makes "give me a fresh worktree on branch X and launch there" possible at all — entire has no equivalent, it only manages sessions, not git worktrees.

And the SQLite index: since it ingests both the checkpoint branch *and* raw `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` directly (per the README), it captures sessions **before** any checkpoint commit exists and potentially after `entire session list` stops showing them as live/current. That's an independent retention layer, not a cache of the same data `entire session list` already gives you.

So the real split is narrower than I first framed it:

| Layer | Keep as-is | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Worktree creation/resolution | Keep | entire has no worktree concept |
| Resume orchestration (fast-path `claude --resume`, fallback to `entire session resume`) | Keep | already correctly layered |

It also wires into Claude Code's hooks to auto-track sessions as they start and stop, and provides shell helpers (`gr`) and worktree-aware resume/launch commands so you can jump straight back into any tracked conversation.

Gossamer ships as the binary `entire-gossamer`, invoked as `entire gossamer ...` once installed (or directly as `entire-gossamer ...` — see [Install](#installation)). It complements entire's own session/checkpoint commands (`entire session ...`, `entire checkpoint ...`) rather than replacing them: entire has no concept of git worktrees and only exposes raw, per-agent transcript bytes, so gossamer is the agent-agnostic catalog, worktree manager, and search layer built on top.

## Installation

**Prerequisites:** the [Entire CLI](https://entire.io) · Git · a Rust toolchain.

```bash
# 1. Build the plugin binary
git clone https://github.com/nosman/gossamer.git
cd gossamer
cargo build --release

# 2. Install it into Entire's managed plugin directory
entire plugin install ./target/release/entire-gossamer --force

# 3. Verify
entire gossamer --help
entire gossamer          # opens the repo browser TUI
```

Entire plugins are local executables, not a hosted marketplace: `entire gossamer` works because Entire finds an `entire-gossamer` binary in its managed plugin directory or on `$PATH`. `entire plugin install` symlinks the binary you point it at into that managed directory (which Entire also prepends to `$PATH`), so `entire-gossamer ...` works directly too, without going through `entire`.

npm install -g .

npx gossamer-skill

cd ~/code/my-repo

6. Adds the repo to gossamer's database.

Requires a git repo with an `origin` remote. Safe to re-run — re-running after upgrading from a pre-plugin install also migrates any existing Claude Code hooks from the old `gossamer ...` commands to `entire-gossamer ...` in place.
